newsitem.title: UK: Expected Norwich share price up as float looms.
newsitem.headline: Expected Norwich share price up as float looms.

text.p: The expected first-day closing price for shares in British insurer Norwich Union rose on Friday, with betting suggesting the shares will close around 350p after Monday's flotation.

Betting at bookmakers City Index suggests a closing price of between 343 and 353, compared with a range of 335 and 345 on Thursday. At rival bookmakers IG Index, betting suggested an even higher close of between 350 and 358 pence.
With Norwich expecting the public offer price to be between 240 and 290 pence, those who manage to secure shares are likely to be assured of large initial profits.
The flotation is expected to value the company at around 5.5 billion pounds and create Britain's third-largest quoted insurer behind Prudential Corp Plc and Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc.
Prudential shares dropped 14-1/2p to 628 by 1408 GMT on Friday, while Royal & Sun Alliance was down 2-1/2p.
"People are taking some insurance shares out of their portfolios to make room for Norwich," one market-maker said.

Shares worth 1.2 billion stg have been set aside for members of the mutual insurer, and a public offer of a further 1.1 to 1.2 billion will be made up of an institutional offer, retail offer and employees offer.
For Norwich, the flotation will bring to an end more than 200 years as a mutual, with policyholders owning the company.
Demutualisation will allow it to separate the group's life operations and thus policyholders' returns from the risks associated with its more volatile and cyclical general insurance business.
It will also strengthen Norwich's financial position and allow the core life business greater investment freedom, analysts say.
